applyMiddleware.ts:54 Uncaught TypeError: middleware is not a function
    at configureStore (configureStore.js:27:1)
    at ./src/index.js (index.js:20:1)
    at options.factory (react refresh:37:1)
    at __webpack_require__ (bootstrap:28:1)
    at startup:7:1
    at startup:7:1
This error occurs when a value passed to the middleware option in your Redux store configuration is undefined or is not a function. This most commonly happens due to breaking changes in newer versions of libraries like redux-thunk or redux-logger. 
Common Causes & Fixes
Redux-Thunk Named Export (v3.0+)
In redux-thunk version 3 and above, the middleware is no longer a default export.
Incorrect: import thunk from 'redux-thunk'
Correct: import { thunk } from 'redux-thunk'
Redux-Logger Initialization
If you are using redux-logger, you must call the createLogger function rather than passing the import directly.
Incorrect: middleware: [logger]
Correct: middleware: [createLogger()]
Mixing configureStore with applyMiddleware
If you are using Redux Toolkit's configureStore, you should not use the legacy applyMiddleware function. configureStore handles middleware application internally.
Incorrect: middleware: applyMiddleware(thunk)
Correct:
javascript
const store = configureStore({
  reducer: rootReducer,
  middleware: (getDefaultMiddleware) => getDefaultMiddleware().concat(yourCustomMiddleware),
})
```

Use code with caution.

Check your configureStore.js at line 27. Look at the array or function you are passing to the middleware property. Print each item in that array to the console; if any are undefined, your import statement is likely wrong.

Can you rewrite this and make it work?
const store = configureStore({ reducer: rootReducer, middleware: (getDefaultMiddleware) => getDefaultMiddleware().concat(yourCustomMiddleware), }); return createStore( createRootReducer(history), initialState, compose(applyMiddleware(...middleware), ...enhancers) )
The error occurs because you are mixing Redux Toolkit's configureStore with the legacy Redux createStore and applyMiddleware. In modern Redux, configureStore handles all middleware and enhancers internally, so you should not call createStore or applyMiddleware manually. 
Redux
Redux
 +3
The Correct Rewrite
Replace your entire store configuration logic with this single configureStore call: 
javascript
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';

const store = configureStore({
  // 1. Pass your combined root reducer
  reducer: createRootReducer(history),
  
  // 2. Set initial state if provided
  preloadedState: initialState,

  // 3. Add custom middleware (Redux Toolkit adds Thunk by default)
  middleware: (getDefaultMiddleware) => 
    getDefaultMiddleware().concat(yourCustomMiddleware),

  // 4. Add custom enhancers
  enhancers: (getDefaultEnhancers) => 
    getDefaultEnhancers().concat(...enhancers),
    
  // DevTools is enabled by default in development
});

export default store;
Use code with caution.
Why this works:
Automatic Middleware Injection: configureStore automatically calls applyMiddleware for you.
Default Middleware: Using getDefaultMiddleware().concat(...) ensures you keep useful defaults like redux-thunk and development-mode checks (e.g., for state mutation).
Simplification: It replaces the need for compose, applyMiddleware, and createStore entirely. 
Redux Toolkit
Redux Toolkit
 +4
Troubleshooting Imports
If yourCustomMiddleware is still throwing an error, check its import source. If it is redux-logger, ensure you are calling it as a function: concat(createLogger()). If it is redux-thunk (v3+), ensure you use the named export: import { thunk } from 'redux-thunk'. 
Do you have other custom enhancers (like redux-persist or redux-offline) that might need specific configuration?

The ERRESOLVE error is occurring because connected-react-router@6.9.3 strictly requires history@^4.7.2, but your project is currently using history@5.3.0. Connected React Router is not compatible with history v5, and because it is no longer actively maintained, it will likely never be updated to support it.

GitHub
 +3
Option 1: Migrate to redux-first-history (Recommended) 
This is the modern, community-recommended path. redux-first-history was built as a faster, smaller alternative that supports both history v5 and React Router v6. 
NPM
NPM
 +1
Uninstall the old packages:
npm uninstall connected-react-router history
Install the new library:
npm install redux-first-history history@5
Update your store configuration:
Instead of using the routerMiddleware from the old library, follow the Redux First History setup guide to create a reduxHistoryContext that provides a routerReducer and routerMiddleware. 
GitHub
GitHub
 +1
Option 2: Downgrade history to v4
If you must stick with connected-react-router, you must downgrade your history version to match its requirements. 
GitHub
GitHub
 +1
Force the downgrade:
npm install history@4.10.1
Verify compatibility:
If you are also using react-router-dom@6, note that it also requires history v5. Downgrading history will likely cause a conflict with the router itself. 
GitHub
GitHub
 +1
Option 3: Quick Fix (Not Recommended for Production)
If you just want to bypass the error and don't care about potential runtime breakages:
Run the installation with the --legacy-peer-deps flag:
npm install --legacy-peer-deps
Warning: This ignores the conflict but does not fix the underlying incompatibility. You will likely see bugs where the URL updates but the components do not re-render.

looking... thank you
The most effective move depends on which version of React Router you are using. Since connected-react-router is deprecated and strictly tied to older history versions, you have two primary paths:
Path A: Modernize (Recommended for React Router v6)
If you are on React Router v6, connected-react-router will not work correctly because it doesn't support the required history@5. Swap it for redux-first-history, which is the current standard for syncing history with Redux [Option 1].
Remove the old packages:
npm uninstall connected-react-router history
Install the modern replacements:
npm install redux-first-history history@5
Update your store: You will use createReduxHistoryContext from the new library to generate the proper middleware and reducer.
Path B: Downgrade (If stuck on React Router v4/v5) 
If you must use connected-react-router, you have to align your project with its strict requirement for history@4.
Force the downgrade:
npm install history@4.10.1
Clean the cache: Sometimes npm gets "stuck" on the old tree.
bash
rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
npm cache clean --force
npm install
Use code with caution.

If uninstalled connected-react-router but still get the following after a build: "Module not found: Error: Can't resolve 'connected-react-router' in 'D:\AHFRR\ahfrr\src'"
This error means that even though you uninstalled the package, your code still contains an import or require statement pointing to connected-react-router. Webpack (your build tool) sees that reference, looks for the package in node_modules, and fails because it's no longer there. 
Sentry
Sentry
 +1
1. Global Search and Remove
You need to find and remove every instance of this string in your source code.
VS Code: Press Ctrl + Shift + F and search for connected-react-router.
Common Locations:
src/index.js or src/App.js: Look for ConnectedRouter.
src/store/configureStore.js: Look for routerMiddleware or connectRouter.
src/reducers/index.js: Look for where the router state was being added to your root reducer. 
Stack Overflow
Stack Overflow
2. Clean Your Build Cache 
Sometimes build tools (like react-scripts) cache old dependency information. After removing the imports, try a "clean" build: 
Delete the build folder: Manually delete the build/ or dist/ directory.
Clear npm cache: Run npm cache clean --force.
Restart Dev Server: If you are using npm start, kill the process and restart it. 
Stack Overflow
Stack Overflow
3. Deep Clean (The "Nuke" Option)
If you've removed all imports but still see the error, your node_modules or package-lock.json might be out of sync.

Can you help me resolve: Uncaught ReferenceError: createRootReducer is not defined at ./src/store/configureStore.js (configureStore.js:7:1) at options.factory (react refresh:37:1) at __webpack_require__ (bootstrap:28:1) at fn (hot module replacement:61:1) at hotRequire (react refresh:20:1) at ./src/index.js (ahfrrTypes.js:16:1) at options.factory (react refresh:37:1) at __webpack_require__ (bootstrap:28:1) at startup:7:1 at startup:7:1 (anonymous) @ configureStore.js:7 (anonymous) @ react refresh:37 __webpack_require__ @ bootstrap:28 (anonymous) @ hot module replacement:61 (anonymous) @ react refresh:20 (anonymous) @ ahfrrTypes.js:16 (anonymous) @ react refresh:37 __webpack_require__ @ bootstrap:28 (anonymous) @ startup:7 (anonymous) @ startup:7
This ReferenceError means your configureStore.js file is trying to use a variable called createRootReducer that has not been defined or imported within that file. 
Medium
Medium
 +1
In older Redux setups, createRootReducer was a custom function often used to wrap your combined reducers with a router history. To fix this, you need to ensure the function is imported correctly from your reducers file. 
Saga Slice
Saga Slice
How to Fix
Check your Import:
Look at the top of your configureStore.js. You are likely missing an import like this:
javascript
import createRootReducer from './reducers'; // Adjust path as needed
Use code with caution.
If your reducers/index.js uses a named export, the import should look like this:
javascript
import { createRootReducer } from './reducers';
Use code with caution.
Verify your Reducer File:
Open src/reducers/index.js (or wherever your root reducer lives). Ensure it actually exports a function named createRootReducer. It usually looks like this:
javascript
import { combineReducers } from 'redux';
// or from '@reduxjs/toolkit'

const createRootReducer = (history) => combineReducers({
  // your reducers here
});

export default createRootReducer;
Use code with caution.
Correct the Usage:
In your configureStore.js, make sure you are passing the history object to that function:
javascript
const store = configureStore({
  reducer: createRootReducer(history),
  // ... rest of config
});
Use code with caution.
 
Redux Toolkit
Redux Toolkit
 +2
Why this happens
In the code snippet you shared earlier, you were calling createRootReducer(history) inside the reducer field. JavaScript requires that any function you call must be "in scope"—either defined in the same file or imported from another.

Redux Toolkit

Would you please help me fix this function: import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit'; import { combineReducers } from 'redux'; import ahfrrReducer from '../reducers/ahfrrReducer'; const store = configureStore({ // 1. Pass your combined root reducer reducer: combineReducers ({ router: history, ahfrr: ahfrrReducer }), // 2. Set initial state if provided preloadedState: initialState, // 3. Add custom middleware (Redux Toolkit adds Thunk by default) middleware: (getDefaultMiddleware) => getDefaultMiddleware().concat(logger), // 4. Add custom enhancers enhancers: (getDefaultEnhancers) => getDefaultEnhancers(), // DevTools is enabled by default in development }); export default store;
To fix this function, you need to address three critical issues: you cannot pass the history object directly as a reducer, combineReducers is handled automatically by configureStore, and the history context must be initialized correctly to avoid the ReferenceError. 
Redux Toolkit
Redux Toolkit
 +3
Fixed configureStore.js
This version uses the modern redux-first-history pattern, which is the standard replacement for the unmaintained library you were using. 
GitHub
GitHub
 +1
javascript
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
import { createBrowserHistory } from 'history';
import { createReduxHistoryContext } from 'redux-first-history';
import ahfrrReducer from '../reducers/ahfrrReducer';
import logger from 'redux-logger'; // Ensure this is imported

// 1. Initialize the history context
const { createReduxHistory, routerMiddleware, routerReducer } = createReduxHistoryContext({ 
  history: createBrowserHistory() 
});

const store = configureStore({
  // 2. Redux Toolkit calls combineReducers automatically if you pass an object
  reducer: {
    router: routerReducer, // Use the specialized router reducer, NOT the history object
    ahfrr: ahfrrReducer
  },
  
  // 3. Set your initial state
  preloadedState: window.__PRELOADED_STATE__ || {}, 

  // 4. Add the specialized routerMiddleware
  middleware: (getDefaultMiddleware) => 
    getDefaultMiddleware().concat(routerMiddleware, logger),

  // DevTools and Enhancers are handled automatically; only add if you have custom ones
});

// 5. Create the history object to be used in your Router component
export const history = createReduxHistory(store);
export default store;
Use code with caution.
Key Corrections Made:
Router State: Replaced router: history with router: routerReducer. A Redux state must be a plain object, and the history object is a complex class instance that would break Redux.
Automatic Combination: Removed the manual combineReducers call. configureStore accepts a mapping object and combines them for you internally.
Middleware Inclusion: Added routerMiddleware. This is what allows your Redux actions to actually change the URL in the browser.
History Export: Added export const history. You will need to import this specific history object into your index.js to wrap your app in a <HistoryRouter> (for React Router v6) or a standard <Router> (for v5). 
NPM
NPM
 +4
